alt.en: A hand-coloured photograph looking up into an old cherry tree in full bloom: thick, rough trunks and long branches covered in pale pink blossom against a pale sky. A small negative number, 39, shows at the lower left.
alt.es: Fotografía coloreada a mano que mira hacia arriba, a un viejo cerezo en plena floración: troncos gruesos y ásperos y largas ramas cubiertas de flores rosa pálido contra un cielo claro. Abajo a la izquierda se ve un pequeño número de negativo, 39.

caption.en: A great cherry tree in flower, in a hand-coloured albumen print made in Japan between about 1870 and 1900, its mount labelled, in the museum's reading, "the great cherry tree of Mukaijima": the blossom the song calls everyone out to see.
caption.es: Un gran cerezo en flor, en una copia a la albúmina coloreada a mano, hecha en Japón entre 1870 y 1900 aproximadamente, con su soporte rotulado, según la lectura del museo, "el gran cerezo de Mukaijima": las flores que la canción invita a todos a salir a ver.

source: Grote kersenbloesemboom van Mukaijima in Kyoto (Mukaijima daishu no sakura, title on object), hand-coloured albumen print, 210 x 267 mm, anonymous photographer; from a leporello album of 30 photographs of sights in Japan
licenceEvidence: Rijksmuseum record (http://hdl.handle.net/10934/RM0001.COLLECT.276388, resolving to https://id.rijksmuseum.nl/200345813): the digital image is subject to https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/ and the object carries the Public Domain Mark (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Photograph by an anonymous photographer, about 1870 to 1900 (see rights.md).

alt.en: A printed page of English text headed "Preface." in black-letter type, over a small scrolled rule. Five paragraphs follow, the first beginning "The present collection consists of those pieces of Japanese popular Koto music"; the last names S. Isawa as director, Y. Satomi and I. Kabe for the selection of the words, and six musicians for the selection of the music. It is signed off "Tōkyō, September, 1st., 1888."
alt.es: Una página impresa de texto en inglés con el encabezado "Preface." en letra gótica, sobre una pequeña línea con volutas. Siguen cinco párrafos, el primero empieza "The present collection consists of those pieces of Japanese popular Koto music"; el último nombra a S. Isawa como director, a Y. Satomi e I. Kabe para la elección de las letras y a seis músicos para la elección de la música. Al pie dice "Tōkyō, September, 1st., 1888."

caption.en: The English preface of the Sōkyokushū, the Ministry of Education's koto book (Tokyo, 1888), dated 1 September 1888: its pieces are "first steps to learning the Koto", and where old words and tunes were "liable to offend the public feelings", "pure and elegant ones" were put in their place.
caption.es: El prefacio en inglés del Sōkyokushū, el libro de koto del Ministerio de Educación (Tokio, 1888), fechado el 1 de septiembre de 1888: sus piezas son "primeros pasos en el aprendizaje del koto", y donde las letras y melodías antiguas "podían ofender los sentimientos del público", se pusieron en su lugar "otras puras y elegantes".

source: Monbushō Ongaku Torishirabe Gakari, comp., Sōkyokushū (Collection of Japanese Koto Music), Tokyo: Monbushō Henshūkyoku, 28 October 1888, English Preface, dated 1 September 1888 (frame 21, right-hand page)
licenceEvidence: Published Tokyo, 28 October 1888, by the Ministry of Education; NDL IIIF manifest "Access Restrictions: PDM"; NDL's reuse page: content with this use status "is in the public domain and may be reused freely" (https://www.ndl.go.jp/en/use/reproduction/index.html). The preface is unsigned, written under S. Isawa (died 1917); the only others it names for words are Satomi (died 1886) and Kabe (died 1922). The page holds words only, no music chosen by any of the six music selectors (see rights.md).
credit: National Diet Library, Japan (NDL Digital Collections)

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "( 107 )" and "SAITA SAKURAI.": one melody line in 2/4 written out three times, under the headings "In Hirajōshi (F♯ minor). [Written an octave higher than the Koto.]", "In Kumoi (B minor). [Written to actual notes of the Koto.]" and "In Iwato (E minor). [Written an octave higher than the Koto.]".
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el encabezado "( 107 )" y "SAITA SAKURAI.": una línea melódica en 2/4 escrita tres veces, bajo los títulos "In Hirajōshi (F♯ minor). [Written an octave higher than the Koto.]", "In Kumoi (B minor). [Written to actual notes of the Koto.]" e "In Iwato (E minor). [Written an octave higher than the Koto.]".

caption.en: "Saita Sakurai", a beginners' koto piece, in three koto tunings in Francis Taylor Piggott's The Music and Musical Instruments of Japan (London, 1893), p. 107: its tune opens like Sakura's, then goes its own way.
caption.es: "Saita Sakurai", una pieza de koto para principiantes, en tres afinaciones del koto, en The Music and Musical Instruments of Japan de Francis Taylor Piggott (Londres, 1893), p. 107: su melodía empieza como la de Sakura y luego sigue su propio camino.

source: Francis Taylor Piggott, The Music and Musical Instruments of Japan (London: B. T. Batsford, 1893), p. 107, "Saita Sakurai"
library: New York Public Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published London 1893; author Francis Taylor Piggott died 1925, note-writer T. L. Southgate died 1917. Internet Archive marks the copy NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT ("no visible notice of copyright; stated date is 1893"). Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
